chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad dari al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah dari Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī dari Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam dari ayahnya dari Ata' ibn Yasar dari Abu Ja'far (alaihissalam) yang berkata:
Rasulullah (shalat dan salam Allah atasnya dan keluarganya) bersabda: 'Setiap yang memabukkan adalah haram dan setiap yang memabukkan adalah khamr.'
ai.seo_question: Apa hukum bagi semua zat yang memabukkan dalam fikih Syiah?
ai.summary: Hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), narrating directly from the Prophet (SAW), establishes the principle of 'kaff al-karam' (abundance does not dilute scarcity) in Shia jurisprudence, meaning any amount of an intoxicant renders the substance itself prohibited as 'khamr'. It serves as the primary textual basis for the absolute prohibition of all intoxicants, not just grape wine, extending the ruling to any substance that causes intoxication regardless of quantity. This ruling underscores the comprehensive nature of the prohibition in Islamic law, linking the physical effect (intoxication) directly to the legal classification.
